_comment: Devices the panel manages, keyed by MAC address. The entry below is named with a leading underscore so it documents the shape without being read as a device: a fresh install that already knows about a machine nobody owns is worse than one that knows about none. Only devices you have annotated live here; anything else found by a LAN scan is runtime state shown in the panel and never written to disk. SSH credentials exist to install the agent; every other device operation rides the agent's own channel.

_example_aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff.name: work-laptop
_example_aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff._comment_ssh: Written by the panel, not by hand. auth is 'key' or 'password'. Every credential is a reference into the vault (config/credentials/vault.json): key_id names a sealed SSH key, login_id a sealed login. No secret material is stored here, and the sudo password an install takes is typed for that install and never stored.
_example_aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff._comment_client: Written by the panel when the device enrolls. token_sha256 is the hash of the secret its agent authenticates the channel with; the raw token exists only on the device. ai_key_ids names the gateway client key generated for each activated account.
